title: curl -X ... "url" silently fails on bracket-bearing exploit URLs (globbing not disabled)
description: Root-caused and FIXED 2026-09-24 while investigating why our agent missed a real, confirmed RCE (CVE-2019-9082, ThinkPHP 5.0.9, sqlinjection-web-1/172.28.0.3) that the user manually exploited with commix using the exact URL nuclei had already found in round 1 (vars[0]=system&vars[1][]=echo...). tools.py's _run_curl built 'curl -X {method} "{url}"' with no -g/--globoff -- curl treats literal [ ] { } in a URL as its own range/list globbing syntax by default, and this exact CVE's payload (PHP/ThinkPHP array-param syntax) contains them. Confirmed live: the bare curl command exits 3 ('malformed URL'), never reaching the target at all -- not a 404, not a real negative, a silent client-side parse failure with no indication the problem is curl's own default behavior. Every agent.py deterministic escalation (_fetch_and_scan, well-known-path/robots.txt/directory-listing/backup-file probing) and every model-planned run_curl call route through this same one function, so this silently broke recon against ANY target using bracket/array-style query params, not just this one CVE.
design: Fixed in tools.py's _run_curl: command now built as 'curl -g -X {method} "{url}"'. Verified end-to-end through the real ToolExecutor.execute_tool('run_curl', ...) path (identical to what agent.py actually calls) against the live target: real RCE output 'phpkniht' (echo thinkphp | rev, reversed) returned correctly, where the unfixed version returned curl exit code 3.
acceptance_criteria: Fixed and verified live. No further action needed unless a regression is found.
close_reason: Fixed in tools.py's _run_curl (added -g/--globoff) and verified live via a direct ToolExecutor.execute_tool('run_curl', ...) call against sqlinjection-web-1/172.28.0.3, reproducing the real CVE-2019-9082 RCE (phpkniht = echo thinkphp | rev, reversed) that previously failed with curl exit code 3.

title: call_model() has no dedicated timeout and silently discards malformed responses
description: Live-confirmed 2026-09-24, round 4 of an engage against sqlinjection-web-1 (172.28.0.3): the model call at [00:01:04] did not return until [01:09:07] -- a 68-MINUTE stall on a single Ollama /api/chat request (likely contention on the shared Ollama host, which has 25+ unrelated models registered per session notes, not something dedicated to this project). call_model()'s requests.post() uses timeout=CONFIG.EXEC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (agent.py:397) -- 7200s/2hr per .env, a constant meant for long-running TOOL commands (nmap sweeps, full hydra wordlists), reused as-is for a single LLM inference call with no dedicated, appropriately-scoped budget of its own. After the 68-minute wait, the response that DID come back was malformed ('Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 118'), and parse_model_response()'s except branch (agent.py:361-363) logs only str(e) and returns the {"chain": []} fallback -- the actual raw malformed text is discarded entirely and unrecoverable. Confirmed via a direct read of logs/session_20260923_235811.json (23 events, last is a 'decision' event) that the raw broken response is NOT preserved anywhere -- not the text log, not the structured JSON session log. A parse failure and a deliberate empty-chain 'I have nothing left to try' response currently collapse to the identical downstream signal (round_num logs 'model gave up'), with no way to later distinguish 'the model consciously stopped' from 'the model's own output was corrupted and we have no idea why.'
design: Two independent fixes, not mutually exclusive: (1) give call_model() its own timeout constant (something in the 60-300s range under normal load, not 7200s) separate from EXEC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, with a defined retry-once-then-fail policy rather than blocking silently for up to 2 hours; (2) parse_model_response()'s except branch should log the raw response text (or at least a truncated prefix/suffix) via agent_logger, not just the exception message, so a future parse failure is diagnosable rather than a dead end -- and the caller (run_attack_loop) should distinguish a parse-failure round from a genuine empty-chain round in the history fed to the next round's prompt, since they mean very different things (one is a real stopping signal, the other is possibly a sign this specific prompt/context is triggering bad generation and worth retrying with e.g. a shorter context or lower temperature).
acceptance_criteria: call_model() has its own timeout independent of EXEC_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, verified via config; a forced/simulated malformed-JSON response results in the raw text being present in the session log afterward, not just the parse-error message.

title: Model-emitted literal backslashes in tool-call JSON params silently corrupt into control characters
description: Live-confirmed 2026-09-23/24, engage against sqlinjection-web-1 (vulhub/thinkphp:5.0.9, 172.28.0.3). Round 2's run_sqlmap target param, as actually captured in logs/session_20260923_233908.json (verified byte-level via Python repr(), not just a text-render artifact), is 'http://172.28.0.3/index.php?s=/Index/\x09hink\template\x0cile?file=../config/db.php' -- a real TAB (0x09) at the position right after '/Index/' and a real FORM FEED (0x0c) right before 'ile', exactly where the model clearly intended literal backslashes for ThinkPHP's namespace-separator syntax (\think\template\file, mirroring the real CVE-2019-9082 payload nuclei had already found and fed back to the model one round earlier, correctly double-backslash-escaped as \\think\\app in that context). TAB and FORM FEED are two of the handful of JSON string escapes that are also single ASCII letters (\t, \f, plus \n/\r/\b) -- if the model's raw JSON text used a single backslash where a literal backslash was intended (needs \\ to survive JSON decoding), any letter matching a valid JSON escape gets silently eaten and replaced with a control character instead of erroring or passing through literally. This silently corrupted the sqlmap target (real result: 404, page not found -- not a real test of the intended payload at all), and nothing in tools.py/agent.py detected or surfaced this -- the model just saw '404' and moved on, with no signal that its own payload had been mangled before it ever reached the target.
design: Not yet root-caused which stage introduces this: could be the model's own raw generation (least likely, since Ollama's grammar-constrained JSON output per CLAUDE.md's CHAIN_JSON_SCHEMA should force valid JSON, and valid JSON require \\ for a literal backslash -- a model that emits bare \t meant it as an actual tab, by the JSON spec's own rules) or could be something in parse_model_response()/json.loads() legitimately doing exactly what JSON says. If the model's TRAINING DATA/prompt doesn't explicitly teach it that a literal backslash in a tool-call string argument (Windows paths, ThinkPHP/Java namespace separators, regex patterns) must be double-escaped in JSON, this will keep recurring for any exploit needing one -- candidate fix is a SYSTEM_PROMPT addition making this explicit with a worked example, and/or a sanity check in tools.py that warns (does not silently proceed) when a run_command/run_sqlmap/etc param contains a raw control character in the 0x00-0x1F range, since that's never intentional in a URL/shell argument.
acceptance_criteria: Either a SYSTEM_PROMPT fix measurably prevents this in a repeat test with a similar backslash-bearing payload, or tools.py gains a param-sanitization check that catches and reports (rather than silently executing) a raw control character in place of an intended literal backslash. Captured in mnemoria either way as a concrete before/after example, same treatment as kali-network-model-8jq/kali-network-model-twv.

title: hydra http-get/http-get-form reports false-positive breach against endpoints with no real auth challenge
description: Live-confirmed 2026-09-23/24 in a real engage against sqlinjection-web-1 (vulhub/thinkphp:5.0.9, 172.28.0.3:80). Model chose run_hydra with service=http-get, username=admin, against http://172.28.0.3/ (bare root path, no login form, no HTTP Basic Auth at all). Hydra reported all 16 of 16 attempted passwords as valid credentials -- confirmed via direct verification that curl with zero credentials AND with garbage credentials both return HTTP 200, and the response has no WWW-Authenticate header at all (no Basic Auth exists on this endpoint). _detect_exploit_success's hydra regex (agent.py:261) correctly matched hydra's own reported hit-line format -- the bug is upstream of that function: hydra's http-get module has no way to distinguish success from failure against a target that never returns a distinguishing failure response (401/403), so it defaults to reporting every attempt as a hit. This is a DIFFERENT root cause than the already-fixed medusa/searchsploit false positives (kali-network-model-0dv.14, closed) -- those were generic-keyword-match bugs in the detector; this one is the underlying tool being fundamentally inapplicable to the target, and the tool's own output format (which the detector is right to trust in general) is itself wrong in this specific case. The real exploitable CVE on this same target (CVE-2019-9082, ThinkPHP RCE via think\app\invokefunction) WAS correctly identified by run_nuclei in round 1 but never pursued by the model in later rounds -- it pivoted to sqlmap/hydra against unrelated URLs instead.
design: Options to consider, not yet decided: (1) only trust a hydra http-get/http-get-form/http-post-form success line as a real breach if a PRIOR probe (curl with garbage creds) confirms the target actually returns a distinguishing failure response first -- mirrors the 'capture real failure signal before running hydra' discipline already used manually and documented in kali-network-model-4qr.2/4qr.3; (2) flag any hydra run where 100% of attempted passwords are reported as valid as suspicious/needs-independent-verification rather than an unconditional breach, since a real credential list should almost never have every entry succeed; (3) separately, the model not returning to a real nuclei-identified CVE (found in round 1) in favor of unrelated brute-force attempts in later rounds is itself worth a follow-up (may be the same class of issue as kali-network-model-8jq -- planning weakness, not obviously fixable by prompt tuning alone).
acceptance_criteria: Either a code fix (e.g. pre-flight failure-signal capture before trusting a hydra hit, or a 100%-hit-rate sanity check) measurably prevents this specific false-positive class in a re-run against the same target, or this is explicitly deferred to the fine-tuning dataset with this exact before/after example captured in mnemoria, same treatment as kali-network-model-8jq.
notes: CORRECTED SEVERITY/FRAMING (2026-09-24): the false-positive breach was worse than 'wrong data' -- it terminated the attack loop for port 80 before the model could ever act on nuclei's own round-1 finding of the exact working CVE-2019-9082 PoC URL. User independently confirmed the real exploit manually (commix -u against the same nuclei-found URL, real RCE). Investigating why our own tooling never reached this even when tried directly surfaced a SEPARATE, now-fixed root cause: curl's default URL globbing broke _run_curl against this exact URL's bracket syntax (vars[0]=.../vars[1][]=...), silently failing with exit code 3 before ever reaching the target -- see kali-network-model-yka (fixed, closed). With that fix in place, run_curl against the exact nuclei-found URL now returns the real RCE output. The hydra false-positive fix (options 1/2 in this issue's design) is now secondary to a more direct structural fix: agent.py has no deterministic escalation that auto-follows a nuclei hit containing a fetchable PoC URL, unlike its existing .env/.git/robots.txt/directory-listing escalations -- see follow-up issue for that.

title: Multi-turn ratio far below 60-70% target in training-data corpus
description: Design target (confirmed correct per user review) is ~60-70% multi-turn / 30-40% single-turn in the core-pathway portion of the fine-tune corpus, deliberately oversampling the recon-to-exploit escalation weak point. Current actual: 11 verified-sequential multi-turn conversations out of 1184 total (well under 1%). This is the single highest-priority remaining item for the qwen3:4b fine-tune dataset (see kali-network-model-8jq / kali-network-model-83s).
design: pipeline_chain_builder.py's template system (training-data/scripts/pipeline_recipes.py) plus the multi-machine farming workflow (make_farm_bundle.sh, pipeline_targets.json, merge_pipeline_chain_outputs.py) is the intended path -- each stage-1->stage-2 recipe that actually reaches stage 2 (ALLOW_FULL_PIPELINE_CHAINS=true) produces one real 2-turn conversation. Two-stage templates (web_login_discovery_hydra_chain) are drafted but not yet run against a live target. Hand-authored matched pairs like cve_conditional_exploit are the other mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: Multi-turn conversation count in combined_chatml_format.jsonl measurably increases toward the 60-70% target, via either farmed pipeline-chain stage-2 runs or additional hand-authored matched pairs.

title: Attack loop no longer conflates leaked-secret discovery with confirmed breach
description: Live-verified against the real DVWA target (172.17.0.12, engage 172.17.0.12 80): the deterministic recon-escalation path (_scan_content_for_secret / _escalate_directory_listings / _escalate_backup_files / _run_deterministic_preflight) set run_attack_loop's 'success' flag as soon as it found ANY secret-pattern match (e.g. the word 'password' as a PHP variable name in DVWA's own routine config.inc.php.bak sample file) and immediately skipped every remaining round -- before the model, or anything else, ever attempted to actually USE the lead. This is the concrete mechanism behind the 'model stalls in enumeration' symptom: it wasn't (only) the model failing to escalate, the harness itself was declaring victory one step too early and cutting the loop off.
acceptance_criteria: Re-running the same engagement after the fix runs the full 5 rounds instead of stopping at round 1, and leaked-secret findings are still recorded (memory.add_finding) and fed into the next round's prompt as actionable leads, without setting the loop's confirmed-breach flag.
close_reason: Fixed in agent.py: _scan_content_for_secret/_escalate_* now return a 'lead found' signal that is kept separate from run_attack_loop's 'success' (confirmed breach) flag -- leads still get recorded via memory.add_finding and folded into the next round's prompt history (with an explicit instruction to actually try leaked credentials against a login form/db/admin panel), but no longer short-circuit the loop. Verified live: same DVWA engagement now runs all 5 rounds instead of stopping at round 1's leaked config.inc.php.bak. Also fixed a second, related bug found in the same investigation: SYSTEM_PROMPT's own format-example literally showed 'run_sqlmap target=http://10.0.0.5/login.php?id=1' -- the live model was caught grafting that exact '?id=1' query string onto a real discovered path ('login.php', found via a genuine gobuster redirect) in round 3 of the same session, producing a nonexistent URL. Reworded the example to use an obvious placeholder ('CHANGE_THIS_PATH') with an explicit warning against copying it or grafting its query string onto a real path. Re-run after the fix no longer reproduces the literal '?id=1' artifact.

title: web2-1 (172.26.0.3, WordPress 6.9.4 'wp2shell'): weak admin creds -> theme editor RCE, full chain confirmed
description: Manual baseline finding for offensive-pentesting-lab-web2-1 (vulhub/wordpress:6.9.4). Real recon (nmap -sV from kali-agent-box, 172.26.0.3, the offensive-pentesting- lab_default network): only 80/tcp open, Apache 2.4.67 (Debian), PHP 8.3.31. Site title "wp2shell" is a direct hint at the intended chain, confirmed below. RECON (all confirmed, not assumed): - WordPress version 6.9.4 via and RSS feed generator tag. - Theme: twentytwentyfive (stock WP block theme, unmodified). - No custom plugins: wp-content/plugins/ listing empty, /wp-json/ namespaces are all core WP namespaces (oembed, wp/v2, site-health, block-editor, abilities) -- ruled out a plugin-CVE angle before chasing one. - Real username enumeration via unauthenticated REST API: GET /wp-json/wp/v2/users -> id:1, slug "admin". This IS the real admin account (confirmed below), not a decoy. CREDENTIAL ATTACK (hydra with a real wordlist, not a guess -- per established methodology): wp-login.php requires a real wordpress_test_cookie from a prior GET (a bare POST without it fails with a generic "cookies blocked" error that looks like a different failure entirely -- captured this first to avoid a false negative). Real failure signal captured first ("The password you entered for the username admin is incorrect."), then hydra run with the field-order and S=-over-F= fixes already established this session (kali-network-model-4qr's WordPress false-positive lesson): hydra -l admin -P .../top-20-common-SSH-passwords.txt 172.26.0.3 http-post-form \ "/wp-login.php:log=^USER^&pwd=^PASS^&wp-submit=Log+In&redirect_to=...&testcookie=1:H=Cookie\: wordpress_test_cookie=...:S=wordpress_logged_in_" -t 8 Result: admin:admin found in <1s. NOT trusted on hydra's claim alone (this session has a documented hydra false-positive precedent) -- independently verified via a completely separate manual login: real 302 to /wp-admin/, real Set-Cookie: wordpress_logged_in_..., and a genuinely authenticated fetch of /wp-admin/profile.php showing the real admin account. Confirmed real, not a false positive. FULL CHAIN TO RCE (matching the site's own "wp2shell" name): WordPress's admin-level Theme File Editor (wp-admin/theme-editor.php) was reachable and NOT disabled (no DISALLOW_FILE_EDIT). Edited the active theme's functions.php (executes on every page load) to add a GET-triggered command executor, submitted via the real per-session `nonce` form field (note: this modern WP theme editor form field is literally named "nonce", not the more common "_wpnonce" -- tripped up the first submit attempt with a stale nonce from a different session/cookie jar before using one consistent session throughout). Verified with real command execution: curl "http://172.26.0.3/?ss_cmd=id;hostname;uname+-a" -> uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data) 0f6b29345ec9 Linux 0f6b29345ec9 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2 ... hostname matches the real container ID -- genuine RCE, not a canned response. CLEANUP: restored functions.php to its exact original content (captured before modification) and independently re-verified via TWO separate checks after the restore POST: (1) the webshell endpoint no longer responds with the marker/command output, back to normal homepage HTML; (2) re-fetched the theme editor's current content and diffed it byte-for-byte against the saved original (`now == original` confirmed True in Python, not just eyeballed). Explicit two-channel independent verification, directly applying the discipline established after web-1's cleanup near-miss earlier in this same session. This is the third confirmed real breach in the systematic container pass (after DVWA's credential leak and web-1's Shellshock RCE), and demonstrates a full realistic attack chain (recon -> user enum -> credential attack with a real wordlist -> authenticated admin-panel RCE) rather than a single-step vulnerability -- good future training-data material for the exact kind of multi-turn escalation the scripted model currently cannot perform on its own (kali-network-model-6w8).
design: No code change -- manual finding only.
acceptance_criteria: Documented with real, reproducible, independently-verified proof at every step (credential, RCE, and cleanup).
notes: Target retired at its old static IP: 172.26.0.3 was part of the retired compose stack. Good news: wordpress/CVE-2026-63030 in vulhub is confirmed (site title 'wp2shell' + identical vulhub/wordpress:6.9.4 image tag) to likely be this SAME environment, now reachable on demand via vulhub_lab.py up wordpress/CVE-2026-63030. That CVE's own documented exploit is a REST-API-batch/SQLi pre-auth admin-creation chain, not 'weak admin creds' -- worth re-confirming whether this issue's theme-editor-RCE finding is a SEPARATE vulnerability in the same instance or was reached via that SQLi chain, next time this environment is brought up.

title: web-1 (172.25.0.3): confirmed unauthenticated RCE via Shellshock CVE-2014-6271
description:
Manual baseline finding for offensive-pentesting-lab-web-1 (image
infosecwarrior/web:v2), part of the systematic 8-container investigation
following the DVWA patient-zero baseline. Real full-port nmap -sV from
kali-agent-box (172.25.0.8, direct docker network access, no host port
forwarding used) showed only 80/tcp open, Apache 2.4.7 (Ubuntu) -- an
Ubuntu-14.04-era version.

Site content is a static HTML5 template ("Lugx Gaming Shop", templatemo
#589) with no dynamic backend visible in any linked page. gobuster
(seclists common.txt) found only static asset dirs (assets/, vendor/) plus
cgi-bin/ (403, meaning mod_cgi is configured but directory listing is
blocked) and server-status (403, correctly restricted).

nikto -C all (forcing full CGI-directory checks, since default nikto skips
them) flagged /cgi-bin/test.cgi as vulnerable to Shellshock. NOT trusted on
the flag alone -- independently verified with real exploitation:

  curl -H 'User-Agent: () { :; }; echo; echo; /bin/bash -c "id; uname -a; hostname"' \
    http://172.25.0.3/cgi-bin/test.cgi

Real output: uid=33(www-data) gid=33(www-data) groups=33(www-data); real
kernel string; hostname "ed63cf499e1f" -- matches the actual container ID,
proving genuine command execution on the real host, not a canned response.

Further confirmed impact:
- /etc/passwd read via the same vector -- found a real low-priv user
  "infosec" (uid 1000, home /home/infosec) with a user.txt flag file
  (mode 600, correctly NOT readable as www-data -- privilege escalation
  from www-data to infosec/root was NOT found; SUID enumeration
  (find / -perm -4000) returned no output and is INCONCLUSIVE, not a
  confirmed "no SUID binaries exist" -- left as an open question, not
  asserted either way).
- /var/www/html itself is world-writable (mode drwxr-xrwx) -- confirmed by
  writing a real test file via the RCE, fetching it back over HTTP to prove
  it was served, then cleaning up. First cleanup attempt (bare `rm -f`, no
  -v, no follow-up verification) was WRONGLY assumed to have worked --
  independently re-checking via a fresh curl request showed the file was
  still being served (HTTP 200) after the "cleanup." Retried with `rm -fv`
  and confirmed removal via a second independent fetch (HTTP 404) this
  time. Direct, real-time recurrence of the exact unverified-claim failure
  mode documented in reports/stage4_patient_zero_dvwa_20260917.md -- caught
  immediately this time because independent re-verification is now the
  default habit, not an afterthought.

This is now the second confirmed real breach in the systematic 8-container
pass (after kali-network-model-co9's DVWA credential leak), and the first
one found through fully manual work in this new phase.
design: No code change -- manual finding only.
acceptance_criteria: Documented with real, reproducible proof. Privilege escalation from www-data to root/infosec remains an open question for this container, not resolved.
notes: Target retired: 172.25.0.3 was part of the old always-on offensive-pentesting-lab docker-compose.yml stack, now retired in favor of vulhub_lab.py's on-demand model (see training-data/README.md). This finding stays valid as historical record; re-verifying it would need a comparable vulhub CVE environment (no direct Shellshock/CVE-2014-6271 dir exists in vulhub, would need a different target to demonstrate the same class of bug).

title: Deterministic recon-escalation trigger: implemented, confirmed first real automated breach (DVWA config.inc.php.bak credential leak)
description:
Direct follow-up to kali-network-model-6w8, which found the model would not
convert a discovered directory/redirect into an actual fetch even when
explicitly told to (round 2 of that test handed it the "/config/ found,
fetch it" lead in plain text and it ran ffuf/nuclei instead). Per user
direction ("go on 2" -- the deterministic-trigger option from the two
architectural choices discussed, as opposed to relying solely on the
fine-tune), added a code-level follow-up layer that acts on well-known
recon signals without any model call.

Grounded in a real check first (not a guess): manually curled
http://172.17.0.12/config/ and confirmed real directory-indexing exposes
config.inc.php.bak and config.inc.php.dist, both readable as static files
(unlike config.inc.php itself, which executes server-side and returns
nothing), both containing live DB credentials in plaintext:
db_user=app/db_password=vulnerables (.bak) and db_user=root/db_password=p@ssw0rd
(.dist).

IMPLEMENTATION (agent.py):
- _extract_directory_leads(base_url, tool, output): deterministic regex
  extraction of indexable directory paths from real gobuster (301-redirect
  entries) and nikto ("Directory indexing found" flags) output.
- _deterministic_recon_escalation(base_url, port, memory, cache,
  step_outputs): for each lead (capped at 3 dirs), auto-curls it, confirms
  it's a real Apache "Index of" listing (not just assumed), parses <a href>
  entries for files, auto-curls each file (capped at 5/dir), and checks
  content against _SECRET_PATTERNS (db_password, api_key, private key
  headers, etc.). A match sets success=True and records the finding via
  memory.add_finding + cache.record_success -- same accounting path a
  model-chosen exploit would use.
- run_attack_loop: after _run_chain_against_port's model-planned chain
  finishes without landing an exploit, if any nikto/gobuster output ran
  successfully, this escalation runs automatically before the next round's
  model call. A hit short-circuits the remaining rounds.

RESULT (logs/session_20260917_140046.log, reports/report_20260917_140046.md,
target 172.17.0.12/DVWA): engage -> round 1 -> nikto+gobuster (model-chosen,
per the earlier prompt-example fix) -> deterministic escalation auto-fetched
/config/, found the 3 listed files, fetched config.inc.php.bak and
.dist, both matched _SECRET_PATTERNS -- port 80 marked BREACHED. Total
time from `engage` to breach: 56 seconds. This is the first real breach
this scripted pipeline has produced end-to-end (model + real exec, no
manual intervention) across all of this session's smoke tests
(kali-network-model-dxv: 0/10; kali-network-model-6w8: 0/10 across 5
adaptive rounds; this run: 1 real credential-leak finding in round 1).

This directly answers the open architectural question from this session:
the "plumbing" (model tool-selection + multi-round loop + execution
transport) CAN succeed once a well-known lead-conversion pattern doesn't
depend on the model's own judgment -- meaning the earlier 0/10 results
were specifically a model-reasoning gap (can't convert enumeration hits
into fetches), not a deeper structural dead end in the pipeline itself.
Reinforces rather than replaces the stage 3(b) fine-tuning plan: this
trigger only covers ONE specific pattern (indexed directory -> leaked
file); the model still needs to learn the general multi-turn escalation
skill for patterns this trigger doesn't cover (login forms, parameterized
endpoints, SQLi, etc.) -- exactly the "shallow not deep" gap identified
earlier remains true outside this one hardcoded case.

Incidental bug filed, not fixed this pass: run_curl (tools.py) assumes
text/UTF-8 output and crashes decoding binary responses (hit fetching
/docs/DVWA_v1.3.pdf -- "'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xc4..."). Degraded
gracefully (logged as a normal tool failure, didn't crash the engagement)
so left for a later tools.py hardening pass alongside kali-network-model-zmm/z7s.
design: agent.py: _extract_directory_leads, _deterministic_recon_escalation, wired into run_attack_loop after _run_chain_against_port. No changes to tools.py or the NegativeCache.
acceptance_criteria: Documented; verified end-to-end against a real target with a real credential leak. No further code change required to close.
close_reason: Implemented and verified end-to-end against a real target: engage -> nikto/gobuster -> deterministic auto-curl of /config/ -> found and flagged real leaked DB credentials in config.inc.php.bak/.dist -- port marked BREACHED in 56s, the first genuine automated success this session. Confirms the pipeline itself works when a lead-conversion pattern is deterministic rather than model-dependent; the model's general multi-turn escalation gap (kali-network-model-6w8) remains for patterns this specific trigger doesn't cover. Incidental run_curl binary-decode crash filed, not fixed.

title: Multi-round adaptive attack loop: implemented, confirms model cannot escalate recon findings into exploit attempts
description:
Two-part follow-up to kali-network-model-dxv (the first DVWA scripted-system
smoke test, which found the model defaulted to re-running nmap instead of
attempting anything). Root cause of THAT was identified and fixed
separately (see below); this issue covers the deeper structural change and
what testing it revealed.

PART 1 -- prompt-example fix (agent.py SYSTEM_PROMPT, no bd issue filed
separately since it's a one-line change verified inline):
The only concrete worked JSON example anywhere in SYSTEM_PROMPT was
`{"chain": [{"tool": "run_nmap", ...}]}` at the very end of the prompt
(highest recency weight). Replaced with a gobuster+sqlmap exploit-shaped
example. Verified via 3x isolated replay of the exact failing goal string:
100% of the time it now picks real tools (nikto/gobuster/ffuf) instead of
re-scanning. Confirmed again in two full `engage` runs
(logs/session_20260917_132203.log, logs/session_20260917_134535.log).

PART 2 -- multi-round adaptive attack loop (agent.py: MAX_ATTACK_ROUNDS=5,
_run_chain_against_port(), run_attack_loop() rewritten):
Single-shot planning (one model call -> one chain -> done) was silently
discarding real recon findings, since _detect_exploit_success deliberately
excludes recon tools (nikto/gobuster/etc can never count as a landed
exploit by design) but the old loop had no way to act on what they found.
Now: after a chain finishes with no breach, the model gets up to 4 more
rounds, each fed the last 2 rounds' real (compressed, non-LLM-summarized)

empty chain if it has nothing left. Two explicit stop conditions surface a
genuine "breakdown": an empty-chain response (model says it's out of
ideas), or an identical repeated chain signature (model loops without new

vulnerable manually in kali-network-model-4qr):

  model wouldn't even try; this one shows that even when explicitly told
  what was found and explicitly told which tools to use next, it can't

title: tools.py: add cookie/session support to run_curl and run_sqlmap
description: Confirmed missing during the stage-4 DVWA investigation (kali-network-model-4qr): every authenticated multi-step web attack this session (DVWA's SQLi, stored XSS, CSRF, LFI, file-upload RCE -- 5 of the 10 confirmed DVWA vulnerabilities) required an established login session, and the current _run_curl/_run_sqlmap implementations have no way to carry a session cookie at all. This means the scripted system as it stands cannot do authenticated web-app testing, which is the majority of what these known-vulnerable lab targets actually require (per repeated user framing: the web app is almost always the real entry point).
design: run_curl: add a 'cookie' param that maps to curl's -b flag (or -H "Cookie: ..."), and support multiple headers (currently only one -H slot exists) plus multipart file upload (-F) for file-upload vulnerability testing -- both needed and currently impossible. run_sqlmap: add a 'cookie' param mapping to sqlmap's --cookie= flag.
acceptance_criteria: A real ToolExecutor.execute_tool('run_curl', ...) call can carry a session cookie captured from a prior login step and successfully reach an authenticated-only DVWA page; run_sqlmap likewise authenticates via --cookie and successfully dumps a table from a session-gated page, both verified against the real DVWA target (172.17.0.12 in this environment).
notes: Reopened -- this was accidentally closed by an unrelated shell command (a mistaken 'get first open issue and close it' one-liner while filing kali-network-model-8e2), not a real resolution. The cookie/session gap in run_curl/run_sqlmap is still unresolved; ignore the bogus 'placeholder' close reason.
close_reason: Added a 'cookie' param to _run_curl (-b flag) and _run_sqlmap (--cookie flag) in tools.py. Verified end-to-end against the live DVWA target (172.17.0.12): (1) run_curl GET login.php extracted a real CSRF token + PHPSESSID from response headers; (2) run_curl POST with username=admin&password=password + the cookie logged in and got redirected to index.php; (3) run_curl GET index.php with the cookie reached the authenticated-only welcome page, confirming the session carries; (4) run_sqlmap with the cookie against the session-gated /vulnerabilities/sqli/ page confirmed the boolean/error/time-based/UNION SQLi and (via run_command with the same --cookie flag) dumped the real dvwa.users table (5 rows: admin, gordonb, 1337, pablo, smithy + MD5 hashes). Also found and fixed a real, independent bug this surfaced: _run_sqlmap's target URL was never shell-quoted, so a query string with '&' (e.g. '?id=1&Submit=Submit') got split by the remote shell and failed with a bogus 'command not found' error -- fixed with shlex.quote(target).

title: tools.py: add hydra http-post-form/http-get-form mode
description: Confirmed missing during the stage-4 DVWA investigation (kali-network-model-4qr): _run_hydra only builds 'hydra -l user -P wordlist -t threads -I service://target', the classic service-module syntax. There is no way to brute-force a web login form (WordPress wp-login.php, DVWA's brute-force module, or any other HTML-form login) through the scripted tool at all right now -- every such attack this session was done by hand, outside tools.py. Two real, non-obvious hydra syntax bugs were found and fixed manually along the way (see design) and should be baked into whatever this tool becomes so future callers don't rediscover them the hard way.
design: New params on run_hydra (or a distinct run_hydra_form tool): form_path, form_params (with ^USER^/^PASS^ placeholders), form_condition (F=/S=), optional form_header (cookie/session). Build the module string with the EXACT field order hydra requires: url:params:H=header:F=/S=condition -- optional H= params MUST come before the F=/S= condition or hydra throws a misleading '[ERROR] no valid optional parameter type given' that looks like the condition itself is broken. For http-get-form specifically, the URL path and its query-string parameters must stay as two separate colon-delimited fields even though they visually look like one URL -- merging them silently misaligns every later field and produces a false '0 valid password found' with no error at all.
acceptance_criteria: run_hydra (or a new tool) can brute-force an HTML login form end-to-end via ToolExecutor.execute_tool(), verified against DVWA's /vulnerabilities/brute/ finding the known admin/password credential, with both the H=-before-F=/S= ordering and the GET-form path/params separation baked in correctly (not left for the caller to get right).
close_reason: Implemented http-post-form/http-get-form support in tools.py's _run_hydra (target/service/username/wordlist/threads plus new path/body/cookie/success_string/failure_string params), with H= placed before F=/S= and the URL path/query kept as separate colon-delimited fields per the design notes. Verified end-to-end via a direct ToolExecutor.execute_tool('run_hydra', ...) call against the live DVWA target (172.17.0.12) using a real session cookie: hydra found the exact known admin/password credential on /vulnerabilities/brute/ (real output: '[80][http-get-form] ... login: admin   password: password'). Also found and fixed a related bug this surfaced: _detect_exploit_success's hydra regex used \w+ for the service-name bracket, which cannot match hyphenated service names like http-get-form/http-post-form -- a genuine form-mode breach would have gone undetected by the attack loop. Fixed to [\w-]+, verified against both the new form-mode output and the original plain-service output (no regression).

description: User is running a full apt update/upgrade inside kali-agent-box directly. Goal: make sure the persistent box has every tool/dependency SUPPORTED_TOOLS in tools.py needs, plus supporting data (exploitdb, nuclei-templates, wordlists), and stays that way across upgrades.

notes:
Audited this session: all 21 run_* tool binaries (nmap, masscan, gobuster, ffuf, httpx-toolkit, hydra, john, katana, medusa, msfconsole, ncrack, netstat, nikto, nuclei, searchsploit, setoolkit, sqlmap, subfinder, curl, wget, enum4linux) present. rockyou.txt + seclists present under /usr/share/wordlists. nuclei templates present at ~/.local/nuclei-templates (not ~/nuclei-templates -- don't be fooled by the empty dir at that path).

Found + fixed a real regression from the user's apt upgrade: msfconsole crashed outright (Errno::ELOOP in bootsnap's load-path scanner) because Kali's llvm-21 package ships a genuinely cyclic directory pair (/usr/lib/llvm-21/build and .../build/Debug+Asserts are the same inode both ways -- confirmed via stat). Not a bundler/gem issue, not fixed by clearing the bootsnap cache or restarting the container. Fix: set load_path_cache: false in /usr/share/metasploit-framework/config/boot.rb's Bootsnap.setup call (pure startup-speed cache, zero functional effect on msf). Also found postgresql/msfdb were never initialized (no systemd in this container -- docs.MCP-SERVER equivalent gap); ran pg_ctlcluster + msfdb init, and defensively prepended 'service postgresql start' to tools.py's _run_metasploit command since nothing auto-starts it after a container restart.

Committed fix into kali-agent-box:latest image (docker commit) so it survives relaunch. Follow-up: once the user's current apt run finishes, re-run this same binary/db/template audit once more in case the upgrade touches anything else (msfconsole broke from a similarly 'invisible' upgrade side-effect once already -- treat this box's package state as fragile after any apt run, not just first-boot).

title: No deterministic recon-only scope mechanism -- freeform goals always default toward exploitation
description: Surfaced while designing the fine-tuning corpus's enumeration-vs-exploitation boundary: SYSTEM_PROMPT has no recon-only mode at all. 'WHEN ASKED TO EXPLOIT A PORT...' framing and the whole tool-selection guidance assumes exploitation is the goal as soon as any chain is requested -- there is currently no way to ask the agent (via engage or a freeform goal) to enumerate/identify/searchsploit-lookup ONLY and reliably have it stop there, the way _PORT_SCOPE_RE already gives a deterministic (non-model) path for an explicit port restriction. For an unattended, no-per-call-confirmation agent (see README Scope & Authorization), defaulting toward exploitation whenever scope is ambiguous is the wrong direction to bias -- it should default to recon-only unless explicitly authorized to escalate, mirroring how a real engagement is scoped by a signed Rules of Engagement, not inferred by the operator's tone.
design: Two complementary layers, matching this project's existing pattern of preferring a deterministic path over trusting the model with a consequential decision: (1) Runtime: a new REPL verb (e.g. 'recon <target> [ports]') or a keyword/regex detector (mirroring _PORT_SCOPE_RE) for explicit recon-only phrasing, deterministically routed to a path that runs recon + vuln-identification tools (nmap/nikto/gobuster/nuclei/searchsploit search-only) but never reaches run_attack_loop's exploitation tools (hydra/medusa/ncrack/sqlmap --dump/run_metasploit past 'search'/setoolkit). (2) Fine-tuning corpus: every training example's goal text should carry an explicit SCOPE tag (recon_only / exploit_authorized / exploit_conditional-on-named-CVE-or-credential), and recon_only examples should be paired with an exploit_authorized example sharing the SAME recon findings but a different correct continuation (empty-chain/report-and-stop vs. escalate) -- teaching the model the divergence is driven by the stated scope, not by what's merely possible.
acceptance_criteria: A freeform goal explicitly scoped to enumeration-only (e.g. containing 'recon only, do not exploit') reliably produces a chain using only recon/identification tools and terminates (empty chain or explicit stop) even when a real exploitable lead (leaked credential, known CVE) is present in the recon output -- verified against a real target the same way the escalation-conflation bug was verified this session.
close_reason: Implemented deterministic recon-only routing in agent.py: a new 'recon <target> [ports]' REPL verb (mirroring 'engage'), a freeform-goal detector (_RECON_ONLY_INTENT_RE/detect_recon_only_engagement, mirroring detect_scoped_engagement's own precedent), and a harness-level execution gate (_is_recon_safe_step/RECON_ONLY_BLOCKED_TOOLS/_RECON_UNSAFE_COMMAND_RE) that blocks hydra/medusa/ncrack/john/setoolkit outright, gates run_metasploit by content (search-only allowed, use/run blocked), and best-effort keyword-denylists run_command. Verified end-to-end against the live DVWA target (172.17.0.12): a full 5-round recon-only engagement used only nmap/searchsploit/gobuster/nuclei/nikto/httpx/ffuf (including the newly-documented 'nmap --script vuln,http-enum' pathway), rediscovered the same real leaked DB-credential config file three times, and never once attempted run_hydra/run_sqlmap-dump/run_metasploit-run -- the model respected the SCOPE framing on its own every round. Separately and directly verified the harness-level backstop itself (not just model compliance) by feeding _is_recon_safe_step a synthetic chain containing run_hydra, a run_metasploit 'use;run' call, and a run_command-smuggled hydra invocation -- all three correctly BLOCKED, while run_nmap, a run_metasploit search-only call, and a plain run_command nmap call were correctly ALLOWED.

title: Add local_docker EXEC_MODE to remote_exec.py (no SSH required)
description: Surfaced during the stage 4 manually-assisted pentest campaign (kali-network-model-4qr): CONFIG.validate() currently hard-requires EXEC_MODE in {direct, docker}, both of which mandate SSH_HOST/SSH_USER/SSH_KEY_PATH -- even 'docker' mode is SSH-to-a-host-that-then-runs-docker-exec, not direct local docker exec. All real targets this session have been local Docker Desktop containers reachable directly from this machine; SSH was never actually completed for local use (attempted early in the session, dead-ended because the target container had no systemd to run sshd). Every real investigation has instead gone through the assistant's own Bash tool calling 'docker exec' directly, bypassing agent.py's remote_exec entirely -- meaning the actual run_full_engagement() autonomous pipeline has never been run end-to-end against any of this session's real targets. Adding local_docker closes that gap without requiring a working SSH setup anywhere.
design: A third CONFIG.EXEC_MODE value, e.g. 'local_docker', whose remote_exec.run() shells out to 'docker exec <DOCKER_CONTAINER> sh -c <shlex.quote(command)>' directly via subprocess -- no SSH, no daemon required on the target. Reuses the exact same two-axis error classification remote_exec.py already has for docker exec failures (container not found, exec failed, etc.), just skips the ssh argv wrapping entirely.
acceptance_criteria: CONFIG.EXEC_MODE accepts 'local_docker' and validate() requires only DOCKER_CONTAINER (no SSH_* vars) in that mode; remote_exec.run() successfully executes a real command in a running local container and returns the same {status, stdout, stderr, error_type?, recovery_suggestion?} shape as the other two modes; run_full_engagement() completes end-to-end against a local container with EXEC_MODE=local_docker and no .env SSH values set.
close_reason: Implemented and verified end-to-end. config.py: EXEC_MODE accepts 'local_docker', validate() only requires DOCKER_CONTAINER in that mode (no SSH_* vars). remote_exec.py: new _run_local_docker() shells straight to 'docker exec <container> sh -c <command>' via subprocess, reusing the existing stderr-classification logic (_classify_failure) for permission/timeout/not-found buckets, with a docker-specific 'Error response from daemon' check for connection-level failures. Verified: (1) CONFIG.validate() passes with only EXEC_MODE=local_docker + DOCKER_CONTAINER set, no SSH vars; (2) remote_exec.run() success and command_not_found cases both correct against kali-agent-box; (3) real tools.execute_tool('run_nmap', ...) succeeded against DVWA; (4) full agent.bootstrap() -> run_full_engagement() end-to-end run against the FTP lab container completed cleanly (recon -> model decision -> hydra attack -> summary), exit code 0, ~4.5 minutes total, zero SSH involvement. This was needed because Docker Desktop's WSL2 backend does not route the orchestrator's network stack into container-internal IPs (confirmed via a real 'ssh: No route to host' failure with working sshd+keys) -- only published ports and the Docker API/socket are reachable, and docker exec already goes through the latter.

title: Stage 3 (planning only): fine-tune dataset curation for a lean pentest model (qwen3:4b / qwen2.5-coder)
description: User's stated long-run goal: a 'pure decent' small model for this agent, not the current 8B GGUFs. Plan is: 1) build ~10 fixed test scenarios (recon-only, credential-brute, web-CVE-chain via searchsploit->metasploit, port-subset selection, etc.) and run them through both currently-registered models (pentest-agent / pentest-agent-alt) to judge (a) whether the reasoning path taken toward analysis/attack is plausible and (b) whether the model is aware of the full tool surface (SUPPORTED_TOOLS), not just the popular ones (nmap/hydra/gobuster). 2) Record every scenario run through the audit pipeline (AgentLogger JSON + Markdown reports) so discrepancies/blind spots can be sorted through later as seeds for a fine-tune dataset. 3) Base dataset: an existing kali-linux-pentester dataset on HuggingFace (not yet identified/pinned by name here -- needs lookup), augmented with our own scenario transcripts for tool coverage the base dataset under-represents (e.g. run_metasploit, run_searchsploit, port-scoped recon). 4) Target models for the actual fine-tune: qwen3:4b or qwen2.5-coder, trained via Colab notebooks using Unsloth.
design: Not an execution request yet -- this issue tracks the planning/research for a future fine-tuning pass. Two parts: (a) a ~10-scenario burndown test suite run against the current pentest-agent/pentest-agent-alt models to check tool-pathway plausibility and full-toolset awareness; (b) using discrepancies/blind-spots found there to scope an augmentation dataset on top of the existing kali-linux-pentester HF base dataset, targeted at qwen3:4b or qwen2.5-coder, fine-tuned via Colab + Unsloth.
acceptance_criteria: A concrete list of ~10 scenario prompts exists; both models have been run against all 10 with full JSON+Markdown records saved; a written summary of blind spots (tools never invoked, implausible pathways) exists to hand to the actual fine-tuning pass. No fine-tuning itself happens as part of this issue.
notes:
Precondition surfaced this session: neither currently-registered model (BaronLLM-based pentest-agent, kali-pentester-based pentest-agent-alt) reliably invokes run_searchsploit/run_metasploit even with explicit SYSTEM_PROMPT guidance added in commit 3480c6a -- this is exactly the kind of blind spot stage 3's scenario burndown is meant to surface and quantify, not just guess at from a couple of live-target runs.

Audit pipeline note (user's own framing: 'we need to make sure our audit pipeline is solid' before generating scenario records at volume): report_generator.py + AgentLogger JSON already capture tool-chain, params, status, and model decisions per session (see reports/report_*.md for the current shape) -- before running 10 scenarios for real, confirm this captures enough to later hand-label a scenario as 'plausible pathway, wrong/right tool coverage' without re-running it (e.g. does it record the raw model rationale/thinking, not just the final tool-call JSON?).
close_reason: 10-scenario burndown run against both registered models (pentest-agent, pentest-agent-alt) via agent.call_model() directly, no tool execution. Full report: reports/stage3_model_burndown_20260916.md, raw transcript: reports/stage3_results_20260916.json. Key findings: (1) both models show good full-toolset breadth (subfinder/enum4linux/sqlmap/john/searchsploit all correctly triggered by natural-language cues, not just nmap/hydra fixation); (2) BaronLLM invents a malformed masscan target/ports conflation (10.50.0.5/20-65535); (3) neither model names the actual correct CVE-2021-41773 msf module for Apache 2.4.49 -- one hallucinates a fake module path, the other picks a real but wrong (Shellshock) module; (4) structural finding: agent.execute_chain() fires all planned steps blind with no model re-consult, so a searchsploit-then-metasploit chain can never actually use the search results to pick the exploit -- this needs a multi-turn loop to fix for real, logged as a design gap not fixed this pass; (5) freeform natural-language port-scoping ('only ports 21,80,443') is not reliably honored by either model -- the existing port-scoped recon fix only applies to the deterministic engage-command path, not arbitrary goals. These are the concrete blind-spot seeds for the stage-3(b) fine-tune dataset augmentation.

title: dns-1 (172.25.0.5): resolved the armour.ai/dubai vhost riddle from the prior easy-lab investigation
description:
reports/stage4_manual_baseline_20260917.md left this explicitly unresolved: "the armour.ai/dubai vhost riddle chain on the InfoSecWarrior port-80 target (only 'armour.ai' confirmed as a real vhost so far)". This is the same underlying lab image surfaced again in the redesigned container stack (dns-1, 172.25.0.5, Apache 2.4.6 CentOS PHP/5.4.16) -- resolved fully here. Homepage ("Welcome to America") has a hidden

tag after ~400 blank lines pointing to "armour.ai". Sending Host: armour.ai to the SAME IP:port returns genuinely different content (verified by content hash, not assumed -- compared against several other guessed subdomains AND a random control hostname; only dubai.armour.ai differed from the rest, everything else was confirmed to be Apache's default-vhost fallback, not a real distinct vhost). armour.ai's own hidden text points to "dubai" as the next step. Host: dubai.armour.ai reveals a real, distinct static site: "Patidar CTF INC 2020" (an open-source CTF-platform HTML template) with login.html, register.html, about.html, hackerboard.html. Verified this is NOT a functional backend -- login.html has no real

(client-side/ static only), hackerboard.html is hardcoded placeholder data (liveoverflow, CR007, anonymous, ashawe -- generic template sample names, not real intel). No flag strings found in any page source. CONCLUSION: this is a genuine, deliberate hidden-content-disclosure puzzle (2-hop Host-header riddle chain), not a further-exploitable application -- the "vulnerability" is the disclosure itself (an operator-hidden vhost discoverable via a page-source Easter egg), which is now fully documented end to end rather than left as an open question.
design: No code change -- manual finding, closes an open question from the prior report.
